Typically fan-in counts all callers regardless of context, though it's more meaningful when looking at production code being called widely across the codebase—that's usually what indicates a utility function that's genuinely reused.

Let me focus on production code call counts specifically, since that'll give a clearer picture of what's actually central to the architecture.

args.command:
cd /bench/repo && cat > /tmp/count_fanin.sh << 'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
grep -rnE '^func (\([a-zA-Z0-9_* ]+\) )?[A-Za-z0-9_]+\(' internal --include="*.go" | grep -v _test.go | while IFS=: read -r file line rest; do
  name=$(echo "$rest" | grep -oE '^func (\([a-zA-Z0-9_* ]+\) )?[A-Za-z0-9_]+' | grep -oE '[A-Za-z0-9_]+$')
  if [ -z "$name" ]; then continue; fi
  # skip very generic/trivial names to reduce noise, but keep most
  total=$(grep -rn "\b${name}(" --include="*.go" . 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  echo "$total $name $file:$line"
done | sort -rn | head -60
SCRIPT
chmod +x /tmp/count_fanin.sh
/tmp/count_fanin.sh
